entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 87_Sylvia_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 2898 vertices and 5792 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Elevation
entries.finding: Radius minus 137 km, false color over −50 to +70 km; broad shape, not gravitational height.

entries.subject: Position
entries.finding: Retained Sylvia vector at 3 September 2026 TT, shared with Romulus.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 87_Sylvia_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked. Reopened 2026-09-18 because its condition was met: the SPHERE photograph lens rides this ADAM mesh, the model the survey’s rotation record and Figure B.29 describe; the Shape and Elevation views keep MPCD.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Decided 2026-09-18 by the published comparison instead: the lens is prepared from 32 camera-1 frames on the ADAM mesh with the rotation record read latitude-first, and ships on zimpol-published-comparison; the registration stage’s numbers are in the README. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 16 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 509 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.46 (median) against a mirror margin of 1.05; 1 of 16 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. The lens stands on the silhouette registration recorded in the entry above and on the route proven against the Dawn mosaic on Vesta; this test adds no independent check for this body.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.29 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.29, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.953 to 0.967 at our phase, against 0.962 to 0.971 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 6 of 8 columns, one step from it in 2. With the paper’s photographs 0.946 to 0.965. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -0.5 to 2.0° and its model panels at -2.5 to 0.0°. The spin axis we project lies at 85.7 to 86.2° on the sky against 83.8 to 84.3° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 5.298 px mean over 32 frames at our phase; the sweep’s lowest is 5.212 px at 14°. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 1.73° from the published pole. Left out by name: zimpol-20181112-061547. Its limb fit does not settle: after 8 full and 16 half steps the centre still moves 0.55 px, and a lens states only settled centres. The figure does not show it.
